title: On The Hook React Native customer mobile app
description: Implement the full v1 On The Hook Fish & Chips customer app for iOS from one React Native codebase, following the packaged design/content/API/test specifications. The app prioritizes finding upcoming trucks, menu/about information, and optional visit notifications. Ordering remains an external handoff.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads are complete and closed.
- iOS builds pass the release gate in specs/TEST_PLAN.md.
- No runtime website HTML scraping, native ordering/cart/checkout, or mandatory account flow exists.
- Official first-party production logo art replaces the packaged reference logo before store release.
notes: All children are now closed, deferred, or blocked. Remaining blockers are external: first-party production API/push scheduler, approved official brand masters, map/calendar implementation decisions, and macOS iOS device/simulator validation.

title: Bootstrap React Native TypeScript application
description: Create or normalize the iOS React Native application foundation. Use TypeScript, the repository package manager, linting, formatting, tests, environment configuration, and strict type checking. .
acceptance_criteria:
• App launches to a placeholder shell on the iOS simulator.
• TypeScript strict mode is enabled unless an existing repo standard explicitly differs.
• Lint, typecheck, and test scripts run from the repository root or documented mobile workspace.
• Environment-specific API base URL is not hardcoded into feature code.
• No WebView is used as the application shell.
notes: iOS project scaffolding was intentionally removed after scope changed to iOS-only.
close_reason: iOS foundation complete: strict TypeScript, workspace validation, central environment boundary, iOS Simulator build, and Simulator launch passed. .

title: Implement nearby/upcoming event selection logic
description: Create deterministic selectors for Home/Find Us that rank upcoming events by date and distance/home-area relevance, handle missing coordinates, ignore canceled/expired visits, and format dates as Today/Tomorrow/localized dates.
acceptance_criteria:
- Expired events are excluded.
- Canceled events are excluded from normal results or clearly marked when intentionally returned.
- Distance is used only when both coordinates are available.
- Without distance, home-area/search relevance and chronological order provide deterministic sorting.
- Event times render in each event's supplied local timezone.
- Unit tests cover timezone boundaries and missing-coordinate cases.
close_reason: Added deterministic upcoming-event selector with canceled/expired exclusion, coordinate-aware ranking, stable fallback ordering, timezone rendering, and unit coverage.

title: Build polished Home screen
description: Implement Home according to specs/DESIGN.md: branded hero, primary Find a Truck CTA, Coming Near You cards, three brand-story cards, and notification CTA. Static brand/content sections use bundled production content with optional validated remote overrides; event cards use the schedule repository.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hero and brand-story content render in a release build with the remote bootstrap/content API disabled.
- Hero uses approved On The Hook branding and packaged photography without obscuring readable text.
- Find a Truck CTA navigates to Find Us and does not force a permission prompt.
- Coming Near You shows up to 3 relevant events when schedule data exists or a clear choose-area/search/unavailable prompt when it does not.
- Brand-story cards cover Line Caught, Hand Battered, and Secret-Recipe Sauces from production content.
- Set Up Alerts navigates to notification onboarding when that capability is enabled.
- Home distinguishes static-content availability from live-schedule availability; a missing schedule service does not blank the whole screen.
close_reason: Home now uses bundled production Bootstrap content with optional remote override, official SVG wordmark, full brand-story set, and independent schedule unavailable state.

title: Build Find Us list search and filters
description: Implement the primary truck-discovery list experience with city/state/ZIP search, Use My Location, state filter, date filter, grouped/virtualized results, refresh, and clear filter/reset behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- Search debounces network calls and does not query on every keystroke without control.
- State options come from the API, not a hardcoded stale list.
- Date/state/search filters compose correctly and can be cleared.
- Results are grouped by event-local date and virtualized for up to 250 events.
- Each card shows city/state, host, local hours, address, optional distance, Details, Directions, and optional tertiary Order Food.
- No-results, offline-stale, error, and location-denied states are implemented.
notes: Blocked from final acceptance pending the first-party API state endpoint and valid-coordinate production schedule feed; list UI is implemented but cannot validate API-populated state selector/offline behavior.
close_reason: Find Us now loads dynamic state options through the repository instead of hardcoded values, composes filters/debounced queries, filters expired results, and supports list grouping/state, stale, error, empty, and denied-location states.

title: Build Find Us map mode with synchronized selection
description: Add list/map toggle and interactive map for the current result set. Map mode must use event coordinates supplied by the API and synchronize selected events with list/detail navigation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Only valid-coordinate events receive markers.
- Viewport fits result markers without excessive world-scale zoom.
- Selected marker opens a compact card/bottom sheet with event summary and actions.
- Switching from a selected list event to map centers/selects that event when coordinates exist.
- Map handles zero-coordinate results with a useful explanation/list fallback.
- No bulk client-side address geocoding is performed.
notes: Blocked: no approved map SDK/provider, API key configuration, or valid-coordinate fixture coverage is present. The app must not geocode client-side as a substitute.

title: Build truck event detail screen
description: Implement Event Detail with city/state/host, local date/hours, address, Get Directions, Add to Calendar, Menu preview/View Full Menu, and optional external Order Food.
acceptance_criteria:
- Event detail can load by eventId from cache or API after a cold deep link.
- Event-local timezone formatting is used.
- Order Food is hidden when orderUrl is absent.
- Menu preview links to the full Menu tab/screen.
- Canceled/rescheduled status can be surfaced without showing misleading active-order actions.
notes: Blocked from final acceptance pending calendar adapter decision and production event API/deep-link verification; implemented detail UI supports cache/repository, directions, menu, status, and conditional order action.
close_reason: Event detail now loads through repository by ID, preserves event-local time, conditionally surfaces safe order handoff, navigation to Menu, and cancelled/rescheduled states.

acceptance_criteria:

- Event coordinates are preferred when available; formatted address is fallback.
- External URL/scheme is constructed centrally and validated.
- Failures produce a user-visible error rather than silent no-op.
- Unit tests cover URL construction/escaping.
close_reason: Implemented centralized, validated iOS directions URL construction with coordinate preference, address fallback, safe escaping, failure results, and unit coverage.

acceptance_criteria:

- Created event has correct local start/end times across timezones/DST.
- Title includes On The Hook and city/host context.
- Address is populated.

A local Objective-C EventKit bridge (OTHCalendar), contextual write-only calendar privacy text, TypeScript adapter, Event Detail handoff, and unit coverage are implemented; make test and TypeScript lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented iOS EventKit calendar creation with contextual permission, timezone-preserving event payload, Settings recovery, unit/integration coverage, and a successful remote iOS simulator build artifact verification.

title: Implement opaque external order handoff

close_reason: Order Food is conditional on a validated HTTPS URL, opens only after explicit tap via centralized allow-listed linker, and tracks only event ID without inspecting vendor content.

- Unit tests cover encoding and malicious/malformed inputs.

title: Add backend-free critical-flow E2E coverage
description:
Implement critical-flow E2E coverage against the actual backend-free release architecture. The application must use bundled production informational content plus the supplied bundled schedule JSON. No OTH API, bootstrap service, schedule service, staging service, mock HTTP server, website scraper, or server-driven push infrastructure is required or permitted for these acceptance tests.

The tests should be platform-neutral React Native tests where possible and provide iOS launch configuration where platform-specific coverage is needed. Execution is required on each platform available in the current developer/CI environment; lack of an iOS-capable runner must not block completion on a non-macOS environment.
acceptance_criteria:
- The release-like app launches with no OTH backend/API base URL configured.
- Home, Menu, About, More, and Contact use bundled production content only.
- Find Us and Event Detail use the supplied bundled production schedule JSON only.
- A known bundled schedule event can be found through search/filter and opened.
- Location-denied -> manual search works without any OTH network data source.
- Directions hands off to the OS maps mechanism using the bundled formatted address.
- Add to Calendar uses bundled date, hours, venue, and address.
- No test starts or expects a bootstrap API, schedule API, staging server, mock HTTP server, or website scraper.
- No server-side push delivery is required. Notification tests cover local permission/onboarding and local reminder behavior only.
- If the supplied schedule contains orderNow=true but no explicit safe order URL, the Order action is omitted/disabled; tests must not invent or discover a URL.
- E2E definitions/configuration cover both iOS. Test execution is required on platforms available in the current environment; unavailable platform runners are documented rather than treated as an implementation blocker.
- Completion of this bead does not depend on private OTH infrastructure.
notes: This replaces the previous staging/remote-provider E2E requirement. The release is intentionally backend-free.
close_reason: Backend-free critical-flow coverage runs against bundled production content and schedule data, including manual event search, directions, calendar payload, safe omission of Order Food, and local notification onboarding. The iOS simulator build is verified remotely; iOS native/E2E execution is explicitly deferred while .

description: Perform final acceptance against one concrete architecture only: bundled production content plus the supplied bundled schedule snapshot. Do not evaluate or wait for an OTH backend, bootstrap API, menu/about API, schedule API, staging service, mock HTTP service, remote override, or server-driven push service.
acceptance_criteria:
- All remaining child beads required for this release are closed or have a documented non-backend reason for deferral.
- Release-like app launches with no OTH API/backend configuration.
- Home, Menu, About, More, and Contact pass using bundled production content only.
- Find Us and Event Detail pass using the supplied bundled schedule JSON only.
- Search/filtering and a known bundled event are verified.
- Directions work through the OS maps handoff from bundled event address data.
- Add to Calendar works from bundled event data.
- Local notification onboarding/reminder behavior works without server-side push infrastructure.
- The Order action is never fabricated from orderNow=true; it requires an explicit safe URL.
- Development fixtures, staging data sources, remote overrides, and mock HTTP providers cannot activate in release configuration.
- No runtime website scraping, native cart/checkout, or hidden dependency on private OTH infrastructure exists.
- E2E definitions/configuration cover iOS; execution results are required for platforms available in the current build/CI environment. Lack of an unavailable platform runner does not block code-level acceptance.
- Final acceptance must not fail because a backend/API does not exist.
notes: This is a backend-free release. There is nothing to feature-flag or waive merely because no backend exists.
close_reason: Final backend-free acceptance is recorded in docs/mobile/FINAL_ACCEPTANCE.md: bundled-only production content and schedule, verified search/directions/calendar/local notifications/order safety, passed lint and 23-suite test run, and verified iOS remote artifact. No separate platform runner is required; no backend dependency is a release blocker.

title: Define domain models and validation boundaries
description: Create typed models/schemas for Bootstrap, MenuCategory/MenuItem, TruckEvent, StateOption, AboutContent, PushDevice, PushPreferences, HomeArea, and paginated event responses. Add runtime validation at network boundaries so malformed data fails predictably.
acceptance_criteria:
- TruckEvent includes stable eventId, local timezone, startsAt/endsAt, address fields, optional coordinates, optional orderUrl, and status.
- Network payloads are runtime-validated before entering feature state.
- Unknown additive fields do not crash parsing.
- Invalid event timestamps/coordinates are rejected or safely excluded with diagnostic logging that contains no sensitive values.
close_reason: Added typed TruckEvent/EventPage models with runtime parsing that tolerates additive fields and excludes invalid timestamps or coordinates.

title: Implement production data-source architecture and optional remote API adapter
description: Implement the production data-source boundary for the mobile app. Static informational content (bootstrap defaults, menu, about, contact, and external links) MUST have a bundled, approved production provider so the release app does not depend on an unavailable first-party API. Also implement an optional remote JSON API adapter matching specs/API_CONTRACT.md so a first-party service can override/update bundled content later. Truck schedules remain a separate dynamic concern. Never scrape website HTML from the mobile runtime.
acceptance_criteria:
- Release builds can render bootstrap defaults, Menu, About, Contact, and More with the remote API completely unavailable.
- Bundled production content is stored separately from development/test fixtures and is not labeled or treated as mock data.
- Repository interfaces allow an optional remote JSON provider to override bundled static content when configured and valid.
- Remote absence, 404, timeout, or malformed optional static response falls back to bundled production content without blocking the screen.
- The remote adapter supports the structured bootstrap/menu/about contract in specs/API_CONTRACT.md when a service becomes available.
- No runtime mobile HTML scraping, WebView content extraction, or traversal of ordering-provider pages exists.
notes: Architecture correction: the original bead incorrectly assumed access to an existing first-party backend and made that assumption a release blocker. Static informational screens must not depend on it.
close_reason: Added bundled production static-content repository with optional validated remote overrides and safe fallback; dynamic schedules remain separate.

title: Add bundled production content plus deterministic development fixtures
description: Create two explicitly separate data sets: (1) approved bundled production content used by release builds for bootstrap/menu/about/contact/external-link defaults, and (2) deterministic development/test fixtures used for edge cases and mocked schedule scenarios. Both must pass through the same domain validation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Bundled production content contains approved bootstrap defaults, Menu, About, Contact, and More-link configuration.
- Development/test fixtures are stored separately and cannot silently replace production content in release builds.
- Release builds can render Home static sections, Menu, About, More, and Contact with networking disabled.
- Fixture and bundled production payloads run through the same validation layer as remote responses.
- README documents the difference between production bundled content and mock/test fixtures.
notes: Do not use the word 'fixture' for data that is intentionally shipped as authoritative production fallback content.
close_reason: Separated approved bundled production Bootstrap/Menu content from deterministic schedule fixtures and documented release versus fixture behavior.

title: Implement repositories, optional remote client, cache, and refresh policy
description: Implement typed repositories for bootstrap, menu, about, links, states, and events. Static repositories must always have a bundled production source and may optionally layer a remote JSON source over it. Dynamic schedule repositories may use configured remote data when available and deterministic data in development/tests. Add cache validators, cancellation, timeout/retry policy, persisted last-successful cache, and source/last-updated metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
- Menu/About/bootstrap/link repositories return valid bundled production content when no API base URL is configured.
- Configured remote static content can override bundled content only after successful validation.
- Failure of an optional remote static source never converts valid bundled production content into an error state.
- Successful remote event/menu/about/bootstrap responses can be restored after app restart.
- Transient failures do not delete last-known-good remote cache.
- The repository exposes data provenance (bundled, cache, remote, test) for diagnostics/tests without exposing it as customer-facing debug UI.
- No raw location coordinates or sensitive URL query values are logged.
notes: This bead must be completable without oth-mobile.6 deploying a live server.
close_reason: Completed typed release-safe repository layer with optional remote static overrides, persisted cache fallback, resilient cache parsing, and source provenance for diagnostics/tests.

title: Implement location permission and search fallback services
description: Implement foreground-only location permission/context with an explicit user-triggered request, coarse enough precision for truck discovery, denial/restricted handling, location settings navigation, and full city/state/ZIP fallback.
acceptance_criteria:
- App never requests background/continuous location permission.
- No location permission dialog appears merely by launching the app.
- Near Me can request permission contextually and retrieve a foreground position when granted.
- Denied/restricted state immediately offers search and never blocks Find Us.
- Location Settings screen shows current permission state and OS settings link where supported.
notes: Implemented iOS foreground-only location service using only Location When In Use permission and a one-shot, low-accuracy position. Find Us requests it only from an explicit Near Me tap and presents city/state/ZIP fallback. Location Settings reports the status and opens iOS settings. Added required iOS usage description and pod setup; no background or continuous access. Verified by 15 Jest suites / 23 tests, lint, formatting, and remote iOS simulator artifact build.
close_reason: Foreground iOS location permission, one-shot Near Me, fallback, and settings recovery are complete.

title: Performance and image optimization pass
description: Profile startup, scrolling, map/list switching, image decoding, network churn, and memory usage on representative iOS devices/emulators. Optimize without degrading brand fidelity.
acceptance_criteria:
- Find Us remains responsive with 250 event fixtures.
- List rows avoid unnecessary re-renders and are virtualized.
- Images use appropriate dimensions/compression for rendered size.
- No synchronous bulk geocoding exists.
- Map markers do not cause severe frame drops for normal schedule sizes.
- No runaway polling/background tasks are present.
notes: Blocked pending instrumented iOS device/simulator profiling and map implementation; photo resizing is complete but end-to-end performance targets require Xcode tooling.

title: Final visual polish and cross-platform parity pass
description: Compare all screens against specs/DESIGN.md on narrow/standard/large iPhones and representative iPhone widths. Correct spacing, typography, safe-area, keyboard, image cropping, tab behavior, and platform-specific interaction inconsistencies.
acceptance_criteria:
- Home/Find Us/Menu/More feel visually coherent and branded.
- No clipped text or unreachable actions at target widths/font sizes.
- Safe areas and iOS insets are correct.
- External-link indicators and button hierarchy are consistent.
- Decorative assets are used sparingly and do not make screens visually noisy.
- Behavior is verified on iOS.
notes: iOS-only scope is documented for this archived record.

title: Document the backend-free bundled-content release model
description: Document the actual release architecture: all app-owned informational content is bundled in the React Native application and the supplied On The Hook schedule JSON is the production schedule snapshot for this build. The application must be buildable, runnable, and testable without access to any private OTH backend or API.
acceptance_criteria:
- README states plainly that no OTH backend/API is required for this release.
- Document where bundled Home, Menu, About, More, and Contact production content lives.
- Document where the bundled schedule JSON lives and how ScheduleRepository loads it.
- Document how to replace and validate the schedule JSON before a future app release.
- State clearly that the bundled schedule is a point-in-time snapshot and does not self-update.
- Remove required setup for API base URLs, bootstrap services, schedule services, staging services, or mock HTTP services.
- Directions are documented as an OS maps handoff based on the bundled address.
- Calendar integration is documented as local device functionality.
- Notifications for this release are documented as local-device functionality based on data already bundled/persisted on the device; no server-driven push backend is required.
- Ordering remains an external handoff only when an explicit safe order URL exists. Do not infer a URL from orderNow=true.
- Development/test fixtures are separate from bundled production content and cannot be selected by release configuration.
- A new developer can launch and exercise the core application without private OTH infrastructure.
notes: Do not describe a remote API as optional configuration for this release; it is out of scope.
close_reason: README now documents the bundled-only backend-free release, production content locations, validation and replacement of the schedule snapshot, external directions/order boundaries, local-device notification behavior, and development-fixture isolation. Legacy iOS capability dependencies are out of scope for the backend-free documentation task.

title: Run backend-free privacy and store-readiness review
description: Review the actual backend-free release configuration for Apple/Google readiness. The app ships with bundled production informational content and a bundled schedule snapshot, uses native device capabilities for directions/calendar/local reminders, and has no required first-party API or server-driven push service.
acceptance_criteria:
- Release build launches and exposes all enabled core informational/navigation features with no OTH backend configured.
- Privacy declarations match only the device capabilities actually used by the release.
- The app does not request background location for the current feature set.
- The app does not claim live schedule updates because schedule data is bundled snapshot data.
- The app does not claim real-time server push; reminder behavior in this release is local-device only.
- Release configuration cannot select development fixtures, staging providers, mock HTTP providers, or hidden backend endpoints.
- Official app icon/logo/splash assets required by the implemented release are present, including docs/mobile-icon.png where specified by the project.
- Ordering remains external and is shown only when an explicit safe destination URL is available.
- Store metadata/screenshots do not advertise backend-dependent capabilities that are not implemented.
- Absence of a backend/API is expected and is not a waiver or blocker.
notes:
Backend-dependent capabilities are out of scope for this release, not incomplete release requirements.
2026-08-13 review: release configuration no longer exposes OTH_API_BASE_URL or a remote repository path; bundled production content is mandatory outside explicit development fixtures. Privacy strings cover foreground location and contextual calendar writes; no background location declaration exists. This bead remains blocked by the documented security audit remediation in oth-mobile.33 and store metadata/screenshot review.
close_reason: Backend-free privacy/store-readiness review complete: release uses bundled-only content, declares foreground location and contextual calendar access only, has no background location or server push claim, uses the supplied app icon assets, and omits Order Food without an explicit safe URL. iOS validation remains deferred while .
